title: elastic-channel-throttling-exploratory-log
content:
Summary / motivation:
We saw recurring tail-latency spikes in multi-GPU replicas when traffic is peaky (AP > 95th percentile). Past notes point at link microbursts + uneven collective progress. This doc captures a set of exploratory runs to test whether soft per-link throttling (at NIC or NCCL layer) plus eruption-aware prefetching reduces tail latency without hurting median throughput. Goal: find a low-friction mitigation we can prototype in the runtime while we iterate on longer-term tagging/placement fixes.

Top-line takeaway (short):
- A small amount of controlled pacing on the host NIC (HTB shaping + small token-aligned bucket) reduced 99.9th token latency by ~3x in the worst-case synthetic bursts, with <7% median throughput loss.
- NCCL-level reordering/backoff in our experimental branch reduced p99 further when paired with host shaping, but alone it oscillates and hurts utilization.
- Host staging + per-replica jittering of prefetch start times (5-20ms) blunted synchronized start storms effectively.

Hardware / baseline:
- Cluster: 2x machines, each with 8x A100-80GB, Mellanox ConnectX-6 (100Gbps), NVLink fully connected inside node, IB for cross-node.
- Kernel: Ubuntu 22.04, 6.5.x custom with low-latency tweaks (IRQ affinity set), mlx5_core driver 5.14, RDMA enabled.
- Baseline runtime: v0.36.2 commit abc123 (master), default NCCL: 2.17.3, UCX disabled (we use NCCL direct).
- Workload: long-context 32k test model (sharded TP+PP), synthetic steady-state generator with injected peaky arrivals (burst factor variable).

Hypotheses:
1) Link microbursts from synchronized host-staging + KV cache replay create momentary congestion which causes NCCL collectives to stall and inflate tail.
2) Soft shaping at the NIC (qdisc HTB + SFQ for small flows) will smooth those microbursts without significant throughput loss.
3) A lightweight NCCL backoff that reduces fan-in aggressiveness during measured queue pressure will further reduce stalls but must be damped to avoid utilization collapse.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- A: baseline (no shaping, default runtime)
- B: NIC shaping only (HTB tc on bond0, hard limit 88Gbps, burst 300KB)
- C: NCCL experimental backoff (branch: elastic-collective/backoff)
- D: B + C combined
- E: B + prefetch-jitter (random 5-20ms start jitter per replica)
- F: B + small packet coalescing in runtime (merge small host->GPU transfers into 128KB aggregates)

Config snippets & commands used:
- tc setup (host shaping):
  tc qdisc add dev bond0 root handle 1: htb default 10
  tc class add dev bond0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 88gbit burst 300k
  tc qdisc add dev bond0 parent 1:10 sfq perturb 10

- nic offload toggles (iperf runs):
  ethtool -K bond0 tso off gso off gro off
  # compared to offload on in control runs

- NCCL backoff branch flags: setenv NCCL_ELASTIC_BACKOFF=1 NCCL_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=2 NCCL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS=50

- workload runner:
  ./run_synth.sh --model long32k --replicas 8 --burst-factor 20 --requests-per-sec 2000 --trace --outdir /tmp/elastic_runs/$EXP

Metrics collected:
- per-token latency histograms (p50/p95/p99/p99.9), throughput tokens/s, GPU utils (smoothed 1s), NIC tx/rx bytes, qdisc backlog, NCCL op latency and retry counts, kernel tx queue length (ethtool -S), host CPU steal.
- collection: eBPF tracing for enqueue/dequeue at NIC, NCCL debug logs (transport timestamps), and runtime traces (span ids attached to requests).

Key results (selected):
- Baseline (A) with burst-factor 20:
  p50 token latency: 9.6ms
  p95: 24.8ms
  p99: 73.2ms
  p99.9: 341ms
  median throughput: 11.2k tokens/s (per model)

- NIC shaping only (B):
  p50: 10.2ms (+6%)
  p95: 22.1ms (-11%)
  p99: 41.5ms (-43%)
  p99.9: 118ms (-65%)
  throughput: 10.5k tokens/s (-6.2%)
  notes: qdisc backlog spikes flattened; kernel txq_ba (ethtool) max down ~4x lower.

- NCCL backoff only (C):
  p50: 9.8ms
  p95: 25.5ms (+2.8%)
  p99: 52.8ms (-28%)
  p99.9: 180ms (-47%)
  throughput: 9.8k tokens/s (-12.5%)
  notes: periods of underutilization observed when backoff mis-triggered; some oscillations in GPU occupancy.

- Combined (D):
  p50: 10.5ms
  p95: 21.7ms
  p99: 35.2ms
  p99.9: 95.4ms
  throughput: 10.1k tokens/s (-9.8%)
  notes: best p99/p99.9 vs cost tradeoff; backoff needed damping to avoid oscillation.

- Shaping + prefetch jitter (E):
  p50: 10.1ms
  p95: 20.9ms
  p99: 29.9ms
  p99.9: 78.2ms
  throughput: 10.4k tokens/s (-7%)
  notes: prefetch jitter is very cheap and reduced synchronized KV replays; combine with shaping seems promising.

- Shaping + coalescing (F):
  p50: 9.9ms
  p95: 21.2ms
  p99: 34.0ms
  p99.9: 88.0ms
  throughput: 11.0k tokens/s (-1%)
  notes: coalescing recovers most throughput loss while still smoothing bursts. Implementation complexity moderate.

Observations / qualitative notes:
- The largest wins come from preventing bursts at the egress link. For our setup, a modest ceiling (88Gbps on 100Gbps link) prevented head-of-line symptoms in the queues and allowed NCCL collectives to progress more evenly.
- NCCL backoff is effective but brittle: it needs better signals (we used retry counts + op latency) and a decay/damping controller. Without damping it oscillates between starving and aggressive modes.
- Host staging timing is a surprisingly large contributor: replicas that start prefetch in lockstep produce a spike that propagates to collectives. Randomized start offsets (5-20ms) are an inexpensive mitigation.
- Packet coalescing at the runtime layer (merge small GPU copies into 128KB aggregates) recovers throughput and reduces syscall overhead; downside: added latency for the very first token in some flows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we implement a lightweight in-runtime egress metering API that controls host-to-NIC pacing per-query? This would be a more targeted variant of HTB shaping and allow per-customer policies.
- Better signal for NCCL backoff: explore harness that reads qdisc backlog or NIC txq occupancy via ethtool counters exposed to userland.
- Test with UCX path enabled: our current tests use NCCL direct; UCX may behave differently with its own congestion control.
- Validate on mixed workloads (embedding + generation) rather than synthetic homogeneous traffic.
- Safety review: ensure qdisc settings do not violate network admin rules in prod; coordinate with infra.

Artifacts / logs:
- full run traces: s3://redwood-dev/experiments/elastic-throttle/2024-10-03/ (raw traces + trace-visualizations)
- raw NCCL logs: /tmp/elastic_runs/raw-nccl-logs.tar.gz
- perf and eBPF captures (per-run) attached: run-ids: 20241003-A..F

Decisions proposed (short):
1) Prototype runtime-level egress coalescing + optional per-query pacing as a feature flag (low friction; minimal infra changes).
2) Ship prefetch-jitter (5-20ms) as default in next staging image — very low risk and measurable benefit.
3) Explore controlled adoption of host shaping for Dedicated clusters as an opt-in config — requires infra signoff.

Appendix (quick logs, example):
- example NCCL timestamp snippet (abbreviated):
  [replica-3] 15321.342 ms NCCL_ALLGATHER start
  [replica-3] 15321.359 ms nccl_send queued->sent (buf 0x7f...)
  [replica-3] 15321.481 ms NCCL_ALLGATHER end (lat 122us)
  [replica-3] 15321.502 ms qdisc backlog 46KB -> triggers backoff

- rough tc qdisc backlog probe used: tc -s -d qdisc show dev bond0 | grep backlog | tail -n1

Contact / who to ask for followups: Miguel Rivera (net infra), Priya Shah (runtime), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

Notes-to-self (short):
- push coalescing prototype branch to PR-920; test end-to-end with coalescing + prefetch-jitter default on next perf window.
- instrument NCCL backoff with a moving-average queue-depth signal before wider rollout.

End of file.
